chain.label: Night conditions at JFK
chain.trigger: Night visual meteorological conditions prevailed at the airport at the time of the incident

chain.label: American Airlines lacked risk controls on concurrent taxi tasks
chain.trigger: a lack of guidance prohibiting the performance of load closeout related tasks during taxi increases the risk that a similar surface navigation error may occur

chain.label: RWSL activation logic illuminates RELs only seconds before a crossing
chain.trigger: RELs will illuminate on crossing taxiways when a departing aircraft has reached a speed of 29.9 kts coupled with an acceleration of 1.20 m/s2, or reached a speed of 49.9 kts

chain.label: Cross-runway-31L clearance issued about 4 minutes before taxiway K
chain.trigger: The instruction provided to the crew to cross runway 31L on taxiway K could have served as a salient cue reminding the captain to turn right at taxiway K if it had been issued closer to that intersection

chain.label: Captain began taxi before receiving the load closeout
chain.trigger: he said that he decided to begin the taxi before receiving the load closeout because the flight had a third flight crewmember

caused_by.evidence: tasks related to the load closeout are considered essential to the safety of flight and are part of required pre-takeoff checks that can be accomplished during taxi

chain.label: Crew head-down on concurrent load closeout, performance and weather tasks during taxi
chain.trigger: The receipt of this information led to a cascade of other crew activities as the captain and FO reviewed and crosschecked takeoff performance calculations

caused_by.evidence: load closeouts typically arrive soon after the airplane pushes back from the gate... he normally made a point of crosschecking the load closeout with the FO and completing related tasks before departing the ramp area

Neither the captain nor the other crew members appeared to recognize how the demand on mental resources imposed by the review of takeoff performance data... could impact their monitoring and awareness of airplane position

chain.label: Captain's surface navigation error: missed turn at taxiway K, continued onto taxiway J
chain.trigger: the captain's prospective memory error in forgetting to turn right at taxiway K, and environmental capture, which prompted the captain to proceed along a familiar, but incorrect, route

caused_by.evidence: the AAL106 flight crew's surface navigation error due to distractions caused by their performance of concurrent operational tasks during taxi, which resulted in a loss of situational awareness
because this clearance was issued 4 minutes before, visual indications were the primary cues of the airplane's position as the airplane approached taxiway K
The night conditions at the time of the incident would have reduced positional cues

chain.label: Crew scanned runway 4L but did not see DAL1943 or read the runway signs
chain.trigger: the American Airlines flight crew's nondetection of DAL1943 on runway 4L likely resulted from night conditions, the location of DAL1943 within a complex array of airport lights, the lack of relative motion... and expectation bias

caused_by.evidence: the captain began turning the airplane onto taxiway J and toward runway 4L... the captain and FO recalled visually scanning the runway, but neither recalled seeing DAL1943
due to the 'extreme darkness' of the evening, he and his FO did not see AAL106 crossing the runway ahead
her attention was divided between crosschecking the takeoff performance numbers and visually clearing the runway, reducing the amount of time she devoted to inspecting the external environment

chain.label: Tower team did not detect the deviation from taxi instructions
chain.trigger: the JFK ATCT team had the responsibility of scanning the runways and airport environment but did not effectively prioritize their duties to ensure a continuous scan

caused_by.evidence: he did not detect the flight crew's surface navigation error and subsequent turn onto taxiway J because he was performing a lesser priority task that entailed looking down

chain.label: AAL106 crossed active runway 4L; DAL1943 rejected takeoff and stopped without collision
chain.trigger: the local controller advised DAL1943 that their takeoff clearance was cancelled, and at 2044:54, the DAL1943 crew responded that they were rejecting the takeoff

caused_by.evidence: the crew crossed runway 4L, where the DAL airplane had just begun its takeoff roll
the crew probably did not expect another airplane to be on the runway and moving toward them

the RELs operated as designed; however, they were ineffective in preventing the crew of AAL106 from crossing the runway 4L hold short markings because they activated too late for the crew to perceive them and stop the airplane in a safe area
Contributing to the incident was the air traffic control tower team's nondetection of the AAL106 crew's deviation from taxi instructions
